rows.subtype: Different ways of relating in toddlerhood [Actor]
rows.description: A toddler may prefer lining up objects, respond less to their name or become very upset by changed routine, and show love in their own ways. Behaviour is what is described here, and a paediatrician can assess concerns.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child may play beside others rather than with them, talk at length about a favourite subject or need a set order for the day. Their way of connecting is real even if it looks different.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A parent may feel worry, confusion, guilt or fierce love after learning their child thinks differently. Connecting with other families and professionals helps them support the child as they are.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, grief, anxiety, guilt

rows.subtype: Social rules that are not obvious [Actor]
rows.description: A child may take words literally, find playground rules confusing and feel exhausted by school noise and effort to fit in. Clear, kind explanations help far more than punishment for misreading cues.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A classmate sees someone who avoids loud games and talks a lot about trains. Including them in activities of their interest, not teasing and asking rather than assuming builds real friendship.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager copies peers' expressions and scripts to fit in, then melts down or shuts down at home. Hiding natural ways takes great energy, and acceptance at home offers a place to rest.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A wise person speaks clearly, gives time to answer, respects sensory needs and does not force eye contact or hugs. Does not treat difference as defect, and asks how the person prefers to communicate.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult may have a deep passion, direct speech and a need for predictable routines and quiet. Strengths like focus and honesty are real, and friendships form easily around shared interests.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: An autistic adult may find open-plan offices, small talk and unclear expectations draining but thrive with clear tasks and written instructions. Asking for adjustments is reasonable, and being understood is a relief.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A bright child stumbles over words, reverses letters and hides books, and starts to think they are stupid. Intelligence is intact; reading is the hard part, and early help and patience protect confidence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
